/SATURDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
Issued at 253 AM EDT Thu Jul 23 2026

This Weekend...

Strong upper ridging is expected to build from the western CONUS 
into the central US through the weekend, with the eastern extent of 
the upper ridge edging toward the mid Mississippi River Valley. 
Meanwhile, troughing is expected to persist across the eastern Great 
Lakes into New England. Our region will be situated in the 
persistent NW flow between these two upper features, while surface 
high pressure from the late week time frame loses influence over the 
area. This will allow for a re-introduction of shower and storm 
chances through the weekend as the stalled frontal boundary to our 
south lifts back to the north near our southern CWA as a weak warm 
front. In addition, could get some weak shortwave perturbations 
moving through the NW flow aloft. Tough to nail down any particular 
timing as differences in individual waves vary among the different 
model suites, however most likely times would be Saturday and Sunday 
afternoon and evenings given diurnal trends. Overall, the low level 
shear profile does not look favorable for organized updrafts on 
Saturday, however there could be some decent flow above 500 mb. Will 
mainly be looking for isolated to scattered pulse storm modes here. 
Sunday could bring more deep layer shear (especially above 500 mb), 
in the presence of strong instability (ML CAPE values over 3000 
J/KG), however low level lapse rates are quite crappy, and LFC 
values will be quite high. Not sure if there will be enough of a 
trigger to initiate convection. If so, we could get some organized 
severe, but confidence is low and data is sporadic on any meaningful 
convective initiation or not.

Outside of the shower and storm chances, we'll also see increasing 
heat and humidity by late weekend as the upper ridge starts to build 
closer to the area. Expecting highs back in the upper 80s to around 
90 by Sunday, with dew points creeping back into the upper 60s and 
low 70s. This could yield max heat indices back in the 95 to 100 
degree range along and west of I-65 for Sunday. 

Monday - Wednesday...

The pattern is pretty interesting for the early week time frame as 
we remain situated in the NW flow aloft between west/central CONUS 
ridging and eastern CONUS troughing. This setup will allow for a 
strongly unstable airmass on the eastern periphery of the upper 
ridge, along with sufficient deep layer shear in that NW flow 
pattern, especially with any embedded shortwave activity. This is a 
classic setup for forward propagating MCS activity assuming there 
isn't too much capping, and that shortwave placement is relatively 
reliable at this range. For the moment, there is plenty of data to 
support the stronger/more widespread activity tracks just to our 
north and east, but given where the instability gradient will be 
combined with enough deep layer shear we could be in the game for at 
least 1 or perhaps multiple rounds of MCS activity Monday and 
Tuesday. Confidence isn't overly high on any one time period early 
week, but the overall pattern suggests MCS activity will occur 
somewhere in the region. Right now, our NE CWA is most susceptible.

In addition to the strong storm chances, we'll also have to keep an 
eye on the building heat and humidity. Right now, Monday afternoon 
looks to be the most oppressive with high temperatures climbing to 
the low 90s combined with dew points in the low and mid 70s. Could 
see some max heat indices jumping into the 100 to 105 degree range 
along and west of I-65. This heat threat could be muted by any of 
the aforementioned MCS activity should it occur. Or, it could be 
worse than currently advertised if no MCS activity impacts our area. 
Stay tuned there.

The same overall pattern could persist into the middle of next week, 
however it does look like temps/humidity will lessen by Wednesday in 
the wake of a cold front and/or convectively reinforced cold pool. 
Will keep some isolated shower/storm chances in here, but overall 
may have a brief reprieve from the worst heat/humidity and storm 
chances mid week.
